svg.text: ERP for Maharashtra Prisons, five government-portal replicas with their own department offices, and the integration bus that links them. Unofficial local demonstration; synthetic data only.
one Node.js + Express process · backend/platform-api · five portal ports + hub
delivered as soon as it is
Dashboard · Received Records · Citizens · Audit Trail
Person Lookup: one identifier (Aadhaar, mobile, CNR,
FIR, prisoner no., name) → everything five systems hold
Identity card · case journey stepper · per-system records
Timeline · live banner when a new record arrives
Same lookup module also runs inside the hub (:4100)
verifies signature · applies each event once
matches the person: Aadhaar → EID → mobile + name
citizen form write-through (both DBs or neither)
5 connectors in parallel, each with its own timeout;
a system that is down never hides the others
live Server-Sent Events to open lookup pages
the ERP’s own database · never opened by a portal
Audit: audit_log (append-only: no UPDATE, no DELETE)
Lookup: lookup_subject (one row per real person)
Read-only migration and backup of both SQLite
Sync Activity and Integration Status pages.
HTTP only: POST /api/intake (write-through) · hub reads ERP API + lookup proxy
A department officer signs in to their own
office (e.g. CCTNS) and registers an FIR.
The record and an outbox event are written
together, in that department’s own database.
The bus sends it at once to the ERP, signed;
if the ERP is away it retries until
The ERP checks the signature, applies the
event once and finds the person across
The record is filed under every person it
Open Person Lookup pages (ERP and hub) show
it within a fraction of a second.

Rules that always hold: the ERP never calls a portal and never opens a portal database; no portal opens the ERP database; data moves only portal → ERP, over HTTP. Identity numbers are stored in the ERP only as keyed hashes and masks.
